note: SEED catalogue — the generic starting set a new brand copies into brands/<brand>/email-sms/email-types.json and then OWNS: usage counts, notes, and brand-born types (a named founder voice, a house subculture) belong to the brand's copy, never here. A TYPE is what the email IS; it belongs to exactly one CATEGORY by one test: whose material is it made of?

types.name: Sale window
types.what: A discount, open for a stated period.

types.name: Launch
types.what: A new product, or a new version of one.

types.name: Anticipation
types.what: Before a launch, and selling nothing. Builds the wait so the launch does not have to arrive cold.

types.name: Restock
types.what: A thing they wanted is available again.

types.name: Bundle
types.what: Two or more products argued as one purchase.

types.name: Last chance
types.what: A deadline they are about to miss.

types.name: Subscription invite
types.what: Turn a repeat buyer into a standing order.

types.name: Early access
types.what: This list sees it first — a membership benefit as much as an ask.

types.name: Gift guide
types.what: Written for the buyer, not the user.

types.name: Problem explainer
types.what: One condition, taken seriously, in their words.

types.name: Routine / how-to
types.what: How to actually use it, in what order, how often.

types.name: Why it works
types.what: The mechanism, only as far as the doubt requires.

types.name: Myth correction
types.what: A thing this customer is told about the category that is wrong.

types.name: Mistake audit
types.what: Three things you are doing that cause the thing you hate.

types.name: The switch
types.what: Against what they used before, honestly.

types.name: Seasonal shift
types.what: What changes for this customer's problem in this season.

types.name: Single objection
types.what: One belief, taken on end to end, nothing else in the email.

types.name: The stack
types.what: How the products work together — cross-sell as education, not as a bundle pitch.

types.name: Moment tie-in
types.what: Something happening in the world this avatar is already inside.

types.name: Holiday, with an angle
types.what: A holiday that means something to this avatar, not every holiday.

types.name: Seasonal ritual
types.what: Back to school, prom, the summer cut, the new-year reset.

types.name: Subculture
types.what: The room this avatar already sits in, regularly, talking about exactly this.

types.name: Regional
types.what: Where they actually are.

types.name: Opinion
types.what: A position on something in the category, taken out loud.

types.name: Customer spotlight
types.what: One named person and what happened to them.

types.name: Someone like you
types.what: A customer matched to the reader's own segment, pain point or state.

types.name: Proof drop
types.what: Several results at once, named, nothing else.

types.name: Milestone
types.what: An anniversary, a count reached, a batch number. Our own history.

types.name: Reader question
types.what: A real question someone asked, answered in public.

types.name: Founder note
types.what: The founder, writing as themselves, about something that is actually true.

types.name: Roll call
types.what: Welcoming the people who just joined, to the people already here.

types.name: Mission
types.what: What this is for and who it is for, stated as a position.

types.name: Behind the scenes
types.what: What we are building and how it is actually made.

types.name: What went wrong
types.what: A mistake, named, and what was done about it.

types.name: Trend
types.what: What is circulating in their world right now — not an event with a date, the ambient thing everyone is talking about.

types.name: The room answered
types.what: We asked, and here is what four hundred of you said.

types.name: Peer advice
types.what: What the guys who already solved this actually did.

types.name: Product spotlight
types.what: One product, what it does, why now. No discount, no deadline — the product is the whole email.

types.name: Risk reversal
types.what: The guarantee as the entire argument. Takes away the reason not to try it.

types.name: Where to get it
types.what: A new place to buy it — a marketplace, a retailer, a channel.

types.name: Channel invite
types.what: Join us somewhere else — text, app, a list within the list.

types.name: Product finder
types.what: A few questions that end on the right product for them.

types.name: Content request
types.what: Asking customers for their photo, video or review.

types.name: Are you still there
types.what: A last email to someone who has stopped opening. Honest about being the last.

types.name: Affiliate feature
types.what: One partner product, recommended with our own commentary and a tracked link — their offer, not ours.

types.name: Affiliate roundup
types.what: Several partner picks in one send, grouped around a theme (a season, a use case, a price point).

forms.name: Designed template
forms.what: Blocks, images, buttons. The default for anything from the Ask well.

forms.name: Rich text with a name card
forms.what: Reads like a person wrote it, with a small identity card. The personal-voice forms.

forms.name: Plain text
forms.what: No design at all. Highest reply rate, lowest production cost.

forms.name: Image led
forms.what: The picture carries it; copy is captioning. Needs the image lane.

forms.name: Text led
forms.what: Designed, but the argument is in the words.

modifiers.name: Rebroadcast to non-openers
modifiers.what: The same email, new subject, to the people who did not open. Already house practice — worth rules rather than habit.

modifiers.name: Awareness variant
modifiers.what: The same type, rebuilt for a different awareness level. Unaware 249 and Product-Aware 26 are not the same email about the same thing.

modifiers.name: Segment mirror
modifiers.what: The same occasion, resolved through a different lifecycle language bank.

treatments.name: Humour
treatments.what: Entertainment is not a category — it has no material of its own. A funny sports email is Cultural; a funny founder story is Brand.

treatments.name: A question
treatments.what: A poll, a survey, a vote. Asking about a product is Promotional; asking about their skin is Educational.

treatments.name: No ask
treatments.what: Deliberately nothing to click. What proves the other four are not a wind-up.

treatments.name: Proof
treatments.what: Photos, numbers, results. Attaches to any category rather than being one.

rule: A type earns its place by being genuinely distinct under the category test, never by filling out a column. A thin category is a finding to call out, not a hole to pad.

arc.note: A slot is a MOVE IN A SEQUENCE, never a standalone send.

roles.earns: Buys the right to ask later. Asks for nothing itself.
roles.sets-up: Points at a specific ask that has not happened yet.
roles.recovers: Runs after an ask that did not land. Never the first ask.
roles.closes: The second half of something already sent.

arc.rule: Cadence is not a rule: no target number of sends, no fixed share that may ask. The arc governs ORDER; the brand's own measured data governs FREQUENCY.
